mechanism: A single 5m bar with return >8x the trailing 24h median |return| AND volume >4x the trailing 24h median volume is a proxy for an in-progress forced-liquidation cascade: leveraged accounts on the losing side of the move get sequentially force-closed at market as price crosses each account's liquidation price. Auto-deleveraging/liquidation engines close the MOST-leveraged accounts first and progressively less-leveraged accounts as the move extends (the 'water-filling'/minimax-leverage structure in arxiv 2603.15963), which mechanically pushes price further in the same direction rather than absorbing it -- the forced sellers (or buyers, for a short-squeeze cascade) cannot choose price or timing, they are closed at whatever the market clears at. arxiv 2607.27070 documents that in the Oct 10-11 2025 cascade 87.8% of forced selling volume landed within 30 minutes of onset and OI cleared 25-70% across 7 sampled cascade events -- i.e. the forced-flow is fast and mechanical, not a diffuse drift, which is what should let a specific spike-trigger separate it from generic volatility.
counterparty: Over-leveraged retail accounts on the losing side of the initiating move, forced to close (or forced-closed by the exchange's ADL/liquidation engine) at market/taker prices they did not choose, sequentially as the move extends through successive liquidation price levels -- not a discretionary trader, an engine executing a leverage-reduction queue.
prediction: In the direction of a qualifying spike bar (return >8x trailing-24h median |return| AND volume >4x trailing-24h median volume, both computed from strictly prior closed bars), price continues (does not mean-revert) over the following bars often enough to clear net cost after fees+adverse selection (c=11.5bps, fee_math.C_BPS) at a 200bps symmetric TP/SL, before decaying back toward mean-reversion once the forced-selling queue is exhausted (motivating a short, ~3h max hold rather than a multi-day hold).

nearest_dead_rows.why_different: Row 6 ('Liquidation-cascade reversion') bet on MEAN REVERSION after a liquidation-flagged bar and was killed for being 'Vol-fade with extra steps; high-vol bars CONTINUE, don't revert' -- its own postmortem states continuation is the real empirical direction. This thesis trades that continuation direction directly, with a precise return+volume spike trigger grounded in two 2025-2026 papers on the actual sequential forced-closing mechanism, not the generic 'liquidation-flagged bar' framing row 6 used.

Row 3 ('1h vol-expansion fade') is also a REVERSION bet on high-vol bars, on 1h bars, and died to single-split selection bias (full-sample -0.187%/trade, Sharpe -2.45). Opposite direction from this thesis, different timeframe, and this thesis's trigger requires a joint return+volume spike (not vol-expansion alone) to more narrowly target forced-selling bars rather than any high-vol bar.

Row 78 ('bb_squeeze_breakout') trades a volatility-COMPRESSION-then-release breakout (Bollinger squeeze), a structurally different setup from a sudden single-bar range+volume spike that proxies an already-occurring forced-liquidation event; row 78 was also refuted for no slippage/drift modeling and TP-hit-rate inflation, defects this spec avoids by screening through lib/screen.py with the required bootstrap CI and cost math.

evidence: arxiv 2607.27070 ('Where does the criticality live? Early-warning signals are event-heterogeneous across seven crypto-perpetual liquidation cascades') reports that in the Oct 10-11 2025 cascade, 87.8% of post-onset forced-selling volume occurred within 30 minutes, and across the 7 sampled cascade events open interest cleared 25% to 70%, evidence the forced-flow is fast and mechanical rather than diffuse drift, and 5/7 events showed a pre-cascade critical-slowing-down signature (2/7, the tariff-news-driven cases, did not) -- meaning some cascades are shock-driven, not all predictable ex-ante, which is why this thesis triggers on the realized spike bar itself rather than trying to forecast the cascade onset. arxiv 2603.15963 ('Risk-Based Auto-Deleveraging') formalizes the minimax-leverage/'water-filling' ADL policy -- the most-leveraged accounts on the losing side are closed first, then progressively less-leveraged accounts as the move continues -- and validates it against the actual Oct 2025 Hyperliquid ADL event, confirming that real exchange liquidation/ADL engines execute forced closes sequentially in the direction of the move (the counterparty mechanism this thesis trades against), not as a single absorbed block.

spec.doa_line: Kill if, at n>=30 train-era trades (combined across the 5-symbol universe), the bootstrap CI95 of net bps (research.swarm.lib.bootstrap_ci.mean_ci, after c=11.5bps per fee_math.C_BPS) includes zero, or observed win rate < p*(200bps)=52.875% per fee_math.p_star(200); also kill if the +-20% tp_bps robustness perturbation (STANDARDS #9) flips net_bps_mean sign between the +20% and -20% variants.

signal_py:
"""Liquidation-cascade continuation proxy. Closed-bar only, causal.

Trigger: a bar whose |return| exceeds 8x the trailing-24h (288-bar) median
|return|, AND whose volume exceeds 4x the trailing-24h median volume, both
reference stats computed from STRICTLY PRIOR bars (shift(1)) so the current
bar cannot inform its own threshold. Signal = sign of the triggering bar's
return (continuation bet, entered at the next bar's open per screen.simulate).
"""
import pandas as pd

W = 288          # 24h trailing window at 5m bars
MULT_RET = 8.0   # return-spike multiple vs trailing median |return|
MULT_VOL = 4.0   # volume-spike multiple vs trailing median volume


def signals(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series:
    ret = df["close"].pct_change()
    abs_ret = ret.abs()

    vol_ref = abs_ret.rolling(W, min_periods=W).median().shift(1)
    volu_ref = df["volume"].rolling(W, min_periods=W).median().shift(1)

    trigger = (abs_ret > MULT_RET * vol_ref) & (df["volume"] > MULT_VOL * volu_ref)

    sig = pd.Series(0, index=df.index, dtype=int)
    sig[trigger & (ret > 0)] = 1
    sig[trigger & (ret < 0)] = -1
    return sig
